audit_items.proof_trace: The RPC computes the toggle direction from the user's last attendance record across ALL dates (no date filter on L43-44), so if a user's previous session ended with type='in' (no corresponding 'out' punch), their first punch of the next day resolves to 'out', directly violating first_record(u,d).type=='in'. No automatic daily logout exists to clear this state: the sole cleanup function performDailyLogout has no cron invocation in the codebase and is manually triggered only. A secondary violation exists: the SELECT then INSERT sequence in the RPC executes under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED without an advisory lock, so two concurrent calls (e.g., NFC double-tap) can both read the same v_last_type and insert two consecutive records of identical type, breaking the alternation invariant.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A user clocks in on day N but the session ends without a punch-out (connection drop, forgotten); since no automatic daily logout runs, their first NFC tap on day N+1 is recorded as 'out' rather than 'in', corrupting attendance records and making the user appear absent for that day's session.
